articles.headlineJa: NBAプレシーズン情報：トレード、最新ニュース、最新の動向

articles.body:
With the preseason games coming to a close soon, the 2026-27 NBA season is less than a week away from tipping off.

How will LeBron James and Jaylen Brown look on the court in their new Philadelphia 76ers uniforms? What will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first season away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their impact this season?

Check back here for all the latest buzz, news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders, with the latest info at the top:

Quick links:

Free agency grades | Trade grades

Trade tracker | Transactions | Offseason buzz

Depth charts | Trade machine | More

Oct. 15

Eubanks suffers torn pectoral muscle

New York Knicks reserve center Drew Eubanks has a torn pectoral muscle and will be sidelined for an extended period of time, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. The Knicks will waive Eubanks, who was competing for a roster spot.

Oct. 14

Clippers waive Christie

The LA Clippers have waived guard Cam Christie, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Christie scored 16 points over two preseason games this season.

Hoop Collective: The biggest questions in the NBA's Central Division

Brian is joined by ESPN's Vincent Goodwill and Tim MacMahon to preview the NBA's Central Division, including the biggest questions facing the five teams. Is this another make-or-break season for the Cleveland Cavaliers? Will the Detroit Pistons repeat their 2025-26 success? And, can Tyrese Haliburton's return vault the Indiana Pacers back up the Eastern Conference standings? 

Topics:

0:15: Our 2026-27 Central Division preview

4:25: Lots of big questions for the Pistons

11:43: Make-or-break season for the Cavaliers

27:50: Can Haliburton bring back the Pacers?

35:30: Bucks post-Giannis future looks murky

42:05: Young talent is intriguing with the Bulls

Windhorst on whether the Cavaliers can improve their roster: "Jarrett Allen is the guy that they would have to do something with. And the thing about it is that they can't trade Jarrett Allen because you'd need a franchise center. And that means Evan Mobley would probably have to be your franchise center.

"First off, if you're trading Jarrett Allen, are you upgrading at center for trading Jarrett Allen? No, you're probably upgrading somewhere else and you're asking Evan Mobley to play center. And Evan Mobley has not proven, even though a lot of people believe that he would be at his best playing full-time stretch center, [he can do that]. That's not something they've been able to get Evan to do consistently well. But that's the move that they have. The move that they have if they have to do something is to look at Jarrett Allen.

"But we'll see how that plays out. The Cavs are in a tough spot in that they are going to be expected to improve on last season, which the pathway to improve on a conference final season, it's a narrow path. And they're doing it in a much more competitive Eastern Conference landscape."

articles.headline: UCL Matchday 2: Viking FK and PSG impress; Man United a mess
articles.description: The Chaaaaaampions! Europe's top competition returned with a ton of goals, a ton of big results and plenty to talk about. Let's start with the tiny Norwegian team that gave Bayern Munich a fright.
articles.headlineJa: UCLマッチデー2：ヴィキングFKとPSGが躍進、マン・Uは混乱
articles.descriptionJa: チャンピオンズリーグ、再始動！欧州最高峰の大会が、大量のゴール、数々のビッグマッチ、そして多くの話題と共に帰ってきました。まずは、バイエルン・ミュンヘンを脅かしたノルウェーの小さなチームから見ていきましょう。
articles.body:
It is the way of the soccer world right now that competitions must get larger, with more teams, more matches per team and a much lower average reading on the jeopardy per match scale.

Aside from the obvious wear-and-tear concerns, I don't really mind this development. (Maybe it's the American in me: I'm used to bloat.)

I don't mind that the Euros have 24 teams, or that the Champions League has 36, or that the World Cup has 48 -- and that two-thirds of the competitors reach the knockout rounds in all of these tournaments. That has allowed for super-cool stories to develop.

Ukraine snuck into the knockout rounds at Euro 2020 (amid growing geopolitical stress) and then upset Sweden. Slovenia and Slovakia eked out advancement in 2024, too, and nearly pulled upsets. And while a huge Champions League with a huge set of knockout rounds has allowed more time for struggling powers like PSG and Manchester City in 2024-25 to rebound from poor starts, it also allowed Bodø/Glimt to find their footing and eventually take down Manchester City, Atlético Madrid and Inter Milan, consecutively, while nearly making the quarterfinals last season.

I don't mind bloat as long as it allows for proper storytelling and extra world-building. In a world with tilted finances, where only a few teams are actually capable of winning the whole thing, a fun journey almost matters more than the eventual destination.

Matchday 1 of this year's Champions League concerned me a bit in that regard. There was still fun to be had -- Como ran away from RB Leipzig in their first ever European group stage game, Real Madrid outlasted Inter Milan in a battle of European royalty, and 11 of 18 matches featured at least four goals. Goals are fun.

- UCL Talking Points: Who's to blame for Man United mess?

- Reaction: Man City can't compete with gold standard PSG

- Kirkland: Real Madrid did win, but glory feels far away

Still, Davids weren't exactly scoring damage points on Goliaths. PSG, Barcelona and Bayern Munich beat Slovan Bratislava, Feyenoord and Bodø/Glimt by a combined 16-2, and debutants LASK, Sabah and Viking all lost by a combined 8-1. It was a foreboding start, a sign that maybe Europe's giants have even further distanced themselves from the pack. I'm a fan of storytelling, and that's the least fun story to tell.

Luckily, Matchday 2 gave us delightful plot twists and track meets.

It also took us to Norway.

Main characters of the week

No. 1: Viking FK

Viking FK has lived a full club life since its founding in Stavanger in 1899: Early regional titles in the 1920s and 1930s; national titles in the 1950s, when that became a thing to aspire to; great spells (four straight titles in the 1970s); poor spells (relegation in 1986 and 2017); the requisite financial overextension in the 2010s (who among us).

articles.headline: Which NFL teams have never won a Super Bowl?
articles.description: Some NFL teams have scored multiple Lombardi trophies, but which franchises have never won the Super Bowl? Check out more information now.
articles.headlineJa: NFLで一度もスーパーボウルを制していないチームは？
articles.descriptionJa: 何度もロンバルディ・トロフィーを獲得しているNFLチームもありますが、一度もスーパーボウルを制していないフランチャイズはどこでしょうか？詳細を今すぐチェックしてください。
articles.body:
It's been 60 years since the NFL and AFL rival football leagues announced their merger and established the Super Bowl, the annual league championship that has been claimed by 20 different franchises since 1967.

Of the 12 organizations that are still looking to capture the elusive Vince Lombardi Trophy, four of them -- the Cleveland Browns, Detroit Lions, Houston Texans and Jacksonville Jaguars -- have never reached the big game.

The 2026 NFL season will culminate with Super Bowl LXI at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, the home of the Los Angeles Rams and Los Angeles Chargers. The Rams, who won Super Bowl XXXIV in 2000 and Super Bowl LVI in 2022 (at SoFi Stadium), opened the campaign at +500 odds to win it all.

Let's take a closer look at the 12 franchises that have never won the big game (along with their number of Super Bowl appearances):

 

Cleveland Browns (0)

There was a time when the Browns were the class of the NFL, winning seven championships with three runner-up finishes in their first 10 years as a franchise. However, it's been a different story in the Super Bowl era, particularly over the last three decades. Cleveland reached the AFC Championship Game three times after the 1986, 1987 and 1989 seasons but lost all three to John Elway and the Denver Broncos -- often in heartbreaking fashion. Over the last 30 years, Cleveland has posted more winless seasons (one) than division titles and Super Bowl appearances combined (zero).

Detroit Lions (0)

The Lions are one of the NFL's oldest franchises (founded in 1930), yet they have zero Super Bowl appearances and arguably the worst postseason résumé in league history. That's why their 2023 run to the NFC Championship Game was such a big deal for Detroit fans. The Lions won their first playoff game since 1992, ending the NFL's longest active drought (and the fifth-longest all-time, right behind the team's previous 33-year winless run from 1958 to 1991). The Lions seemed poised to make their first Super Bowl appearance, but the San Francisco 49ers erased a 17-point deficit and defeated Detroit to punch their Super Bowl ticket.

Houston Texans (0)

The Texans are the newest franchise in the league, having joined as an expansion team in 2002, so Houston's inclusion on this list shouldn't come as much of a surprise. Still, it's been a tough couple of decades for the Texans, who have never reached a conference championship. However, that could change in the coming years, as rookie quarterback C.J. Stroud already looks like a potential superstar, while head coach DeMeco Ryans is a rising star himself and has Super Bowl experience from his time as an assistant coach in San Francisco. Their 45-14 wild-card win over Cleveland during the 2023-24 season helped Texans fans feel hopeful.

Jacksonville Jaguars (0)

articles.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Oct. 15: Nine players to trade for

By Michael F. Florio

Bhayshul Tuten was my guy this summer and I am doubling down now. He has been highly effective on a per-touch basis. Currently, he is fourth among all RBs in missed tackles forced and sixth in explosive runs. He leads the NFL in each on outside runs, and he has scored the Jacksonville Jaguars' only two goal-line rushing touchdowns. He has seen a career high in carries in each of his last two games and tied his career high with three targets last week. Plus, the Jaguars face the Houston Texans this week and then have their bye week, so this may be the ideal time to make an offer. After the bye, the schedule opens up with matchups against the Indianapolis Colts, Tennessee Titans (twice), New York Giants, Chicago Bears, Dallas Cowboys and Washington Commanders.

Parker Washington is another Jaguar you should try to trade for. I know, it's a hot take to say to trade for the WR13 in fantasy PPG. However, I do not think that Washington is perceived as a fantasy WR1 like he should be, so trading for him at a WR2 cost is worth a shot. Washington has been great and the Jaguars have the best remaining fantasy schedule for WRs. While we're at it, trying to trade for Trevor Lawrence, who has been up and down thus far, is worth a try as well.

Luther Burden III has not had a real "boom" performance yet, but he has been a steady source of volume. That has led to him being a "safe floor" play. But I expect we see a lot more ceiling games with Caleb Williams nearing a return. Plus, the Bears have the third-best remaining fantasy schedule for wide receivers, with matchups against the Detroit Lions (twice), New Orleans Saints, Miami Dolphins and Buffalo Bills.

Admittedly, it may be trading for them while their values are at their highest, but if you believe in Packers receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden like I do, it will be well worth it. The Packers will likely have to throw at a high rate all season due to their lack of a run game. Watson is the WR4 in fantasy PPG, yet no one would value him as a top-five receiver. Golden is the WR17, yet I am not sure he will be valued that highly by fantasy managers. So there still is value in a trade. Plus, the Packers have a very favorable schedule, with upcoming matchups against the Cowboys, Lions, Saints, Bills, Bears, and Texans.

articles.headline: Tyler, The Creator joins stars to appear on Barcelona Clásico kit
articles.description: It's become a tradition in recent years for Barcelona to add the logo of top music stars to their jerseys when they face Real Madrid in El Clásico.
articles.headlineJa: タイラー・ザ・クリエイター、バルセロナのクラシコ用キットに登場するスター陣に加わる
articles.descriptionJa: 近年、バルセロナはエル・クラシコでレアル・マドリードと対戦する際、トップミュージシャンのロゴをユニフォームに加えることを恒例としている。
articles.body:
It's become something of a tradition in recent years for Barcelona to change up their kits when they face Real Madrid in El Clásico.

As part of their massive sponsorship deal with Spotify, Barça have been sporting the trademark logos of some of the biggest music acts when they face their bitter rivals in LaLiga matches. This began in 2022, when Drake became the first international star to have his own emblem replace the standard Spotify logo on the front of the Catalan club's jersey.

With the first Clásico of the 2026-27 season almost upon us, Barça have revealed the identity of the latest big-named act who will be gracing their jerseys for the fixture with the honor going to eclectic rapper and fashionista Tyler, The Creator.

The multiple Grammy-winning hip-hop star therefore becomes the ninth musical act to have its logo worn by Barça during El Clásico in the space of the past five years. He joins an exclusive club of acts to be given the honor, including Coldplay, Ed Sheeran and Olivia Rodrigo -- all of whom have seen their custom marques added to special-edition kits in lieu of a traditional front-of-shirt sponsor.

- Watch El Clasico, Oct. 25 at 3 p.m. ET on ABC and ESPN+ (U.S.)

- Why did Manchester City fans bring inflatable bananas to Anfield?

- Liverpool fans 'welcome' City in first match since guilty verdict

2022-23

DRAKE, Oct. 16, 2022 (Real Madrid 3-1 Barcelona)

Less than a year into Barça's ongoing deal with Spotify, with the club's Camp Nou stadium also bearing the name of the streaming giant, Drake became the first musician to have his logo adorn the hallowed red-and-blue striped jersey when the Canadian rapper's "OVO" owl label was on display during a disappointing defeat at the Bernabéu in the first Clásico of the season.

ROSALÍA, March 19, 2023 (Barcelona 2-1 Real Madrid)

Catalonia-born pop star Rosalía proved to be a much brighter omen for Barça, who won the reverse fixture at Camp Nou while wearing the logo for her "Motomami" album across their shirts.

2023-24

THE ROLLING STONES, Oct. 28, 2023 (Barcelona 1-2 Real Madrid)

The Stones marked the release of their first album in 18 years, "Hackney Diamonds," by slapping their iconic lips and tongue logo to the Barcelona shirt. Lamine Yamal made his Clásico debut (played at the city's Olympic stadium as renovations at Camp Nou began) but unfortunately the home side fell to defeat via two second-half goals from Jude Bellingham.

KAROL G, April 21, 2024 (Real Madrid 3-2 Barcelona)

Barça narrowly lost out to another late Bellingham strike, this time at the Bernabéu, while wearing bespoke shirts with the signature barbed-wire heart logo of Colombian singer and songwriter Karol G on the front.

2024-25

COLDPLAY, Oct. 26, 2024 (Real Madrid 0-4 Barcelona)

articles.headline: Spurs debut three-guard lineup of Fox, Harper, Castle in preseason win
articles.description: Spurs coach Mitch Johnson finally deployed a three-guard lineup featuring De'Aaron Fox, Dylan Harper and Stephon Castle in a 123-103 preseason win over the Suns.
articles.headlineJa: スパーズ、プレシーズン戦の勝利でフォックス、ハーパー、キャスルの3ガード体制を初披露
articles.descriptionJa: 水曜日のサンズ戦で123-103と勝利したスパーズのミッチ・ジョンソン監督は、ついにディアロン・フォックス、ディラン・ハーパー、ステフォン・キャッスルを起用した3ガード体制を導入した。
articles.body:
SAN ANTONIO -- Spurs coach Mitch Johnson finally deployed a three-guard lineup featuring De'Aaron Fox, Dylan Harper and Stephon Castle in a 123-103 preseason win over the Phoenix Suns on Wednesday, explaining "it's time to push forward appropriately" the team's "natural evolution that will still take time."

That was apparent in the group's choppy start as Harper and Castle combined to miss their first five shots before Fox, making his preseason debut, subbed out with 6:57 left in the opening quarter.

But by the time the buzzer sounded for intermission, Fox, Harper and Castle had combined for 31 points, 12 rebounds and six assists in helping San Antonio seize a 60-49 halftime lead.

"I'm glad they got to play some together and we got some reps out there," Johnson said. "I thought we started the game with some very sloppy possessions, and everybody will have to have a better start to games and a better approach with that."

Fox drilled a corner 3-pointer with one second left for the Spurs' final points of the first half. Castle led all scorers with a game-high 18 points, including 14 from the free throw line. Harper, who finished with nine points, drew the most raucous cheers from the Frost Bank Center crowd with 34.5 seconds left in the second quarter, when he caught a Devin Vassell miss for a rim-rocking tip dunk.

Fox even slammed home a poster dunk in the first half.

"I felt like we were trying to do the right things at the beginning, but we scored so few points," Spurs forward Victor Wembanyama said. "When it clicked, it clicked. The biggest thing is I've got handlers all around me, guys that we want to put the ball in their hands and pick and roll around me. That makes things easier."

Fox, Harper and Castle spent a total of 11 minutes on the court together in the opening half, combining for 19 points to finish with a net rating of plus-10. Fox, Harper and Castle played only 69 minutes together all of last season, including 25 in the NBA Finals, and opponents outscored the Spurs by 47 points in those minutes.

By comparison, the Spurs finished with a plus-9.4 net rating when Fox and Castle shared the court in the regular season, plus-6.2 with Fox and Harper, and plus-11.0 with Harper and Castle.

Fox said the guards spoke over the summer in France, when they visited Wembanyama, about the prospect of potentially playing in the starting lineup together.

"Obviously, when we were in the Finals, and just throughout the playoffs, there were times where we all three played together, a lot more than we did throughout the regular season," Fox said. "But we knew there was a chance that we'd all be starting or at least sharing the court together. We're all excited for it."

articles.headline: Marc Guéhi hails Man City unity amid financial charges fallout
articles.description: Marc Guéhi hailed Manchester City's unity in the face of adversity after a spirited fightback in the club's first home match since being found guilty of multiple breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations.
articles.headlineJa: マーク・グエイ、財務規則違反の処分に直面する中でのマン・シティの結束を称賛
articles.descriptionJa: プレミアリーグの財務規則に対する複数の違反で有罪判決を受けた後、クラブにとって初のホームゲームで力強い反撃を見せたことを受け、マーク・グエイは逆境におけるマンチェスター・シティの結束を称賛した。
articles.body:
Marc Guéhi hailed Manchester City's unity in the face of adversity after a spirited fightback in the club's first home match since being found guilty of multiple breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations.

City were beaten 4-2 by Paris St Germain in the Champions League on Wednesday but only after a rousing response to being swatted aside 3-0 by the holders in the first half at the Etihad Stadium.

It was a night when City showed their defiance in the face of the last month's damning verdict by an independent commission, which found the club had broken Premier League rules.

Former manager Pep Guardiola was in attendance in a strong show of support for the under-fire hierarchy, who have appealed against the judgement, while fans unveiled a huge "City Til I Die" tifo to make underline their loyalty.

A ferocious atmosphere threatened to fall flat as PSG produced a clinical first-half display but it was reenergised after the break as City produced enough chances -- including hitting the woodwork twice - to threaten an unlikely comeback.

Defender Guehi said: "I think the support that we've had from the fans and the football club has been fantastic and everyone's definitely together in this.

"I think it says a lot about, not just the players, but the football club in general. It's very easy when adversity comes to focus on that, but everyone's been focused on what's in front of them, which is the games.

"As long as we carry on playing like we did in the second half and training well, things will look positive for us."

City were ripped apart by the back-to-back champions in the first half, with quickfire goals from Désiré Doué and Ousmane Dembélé establishing control.

- Man City can't compete with PSG, the Champions League's gold standard

- Man City's Antoine Semenyo on missed chances against PSG: 'Beating myself up'

The game seemed all but over when Vitinha made it 3-0 with 32 minutes gone but a triple substitution by Enzo Maresca at the break sparked a chaotic second period.

Erling Haaland struck twice -- becoming City's record Champions League goalscorer in the process with 38 from 41 appearances -- while also hitting the crossbar and seeing Enzo Fernández denied by the post.

But the task was to prove just beyond City as PSG claimed a fourth when a Maghnes Akliouche effort squeezed past a despairing Gianluigi Donnarumma. Former City striker Ferran Torres also missed a late penalty for the visitors.

Guehi said: "Playing at home, it's not really acceptable, that performance in the first half, in front of our home fans, so I'm just really glad everyone reacted in a positive manner and at least came out fighting.

"For the first goals, they were just a bit more aggressive, won a lot of the 1v1 duels, which allowed them the platform to go score those goals.

"But the second half was the complete opposite. We were a lot more aggressive, won a lot more of the duels, which gave us the platform.

articles.description: Here's a look at what each NFL team is wearing in Week 6, led by throwbacks from the Broncos and Seahawks.
articles.headlineJa: NFL第6週のユニフォーム：ブロンコスとシーホークスがTNFの対戦で復刻モデルを着用
articles.descriptionJa: ブロンコスとシーホークスの復刻モデル着用を中心に、NFL各チームの第6週のユニフォームを紹介する。
articles.body:
Throwback Thursday is coming to the NFL in Week 6 with a matchup for nostalgic eyes on "Thursday Night Football." The Denver Broncos and Seattle Seahawks will each wear their throwback uniforms in the game.

Denver's look is a callback to the 1977 uniforms that honor the "Orange Crush" era. The orange jerseys include oversized white numbers in legacy blue trim, while white pants and legacy blue helmet complete the look. Featured on the lid is the iconic hissing Bronco and "D" on the side. The Broncos boast a 5-0 record since debuting the combination in the 2024 campaign.

Seattle is throwing it back to the 1990s with its royal blue jerseys, and matching silver helmet and pants. Running on the uniform's sleeve is a classic Seahawks logo on top of green and blue stripes. Neatly, the old Kingdome appears on the inside collar. The matte silver helmet is similar to what the franchise wore in its early history. The Seahawks have a 4-3 record in the throwbacks since debuting them in 2023. 

The alternate uniform space is well represented, too, as the New Orleans Saints are wearing their all-white color rush uniforms with a white helmet against the New York Giants. New Orleans unveiled the white lids in 2025 with a new tri-color stripe down the center and a black face mask for the first time in franchise history. A mini fleur-de-lis is subtly included on the tri-color stripe.

articles.headline: Why does Haaland score so many goals? Because he's elite at staying onside
articles.description: We know what a dominant scorer Erling Haaland is, but it often goes unnoticed how good he is at avoiding a striker's worst enemy: the offside trap.
articles.body:
The referees are sorry; they really are. According to the Premier League's official statement, the reason VAR overlooked an extremely offside Enzo Fernández on the goal that decided last month's Manchester derby was that officials were simply too busy watching Erling Haaland.

And honestly: who could blame them? The man is captivating in slow mo.

As Josko Gvardiol scooted up the opposite side of the box, Haaland adjusted each stride to stay perfectly level with the ball: a half-step with his left foot, then a lunge with his right, always landing precisely where he needed to be. When Gvardiol curled the cross around Patrick Dorgu some 30 yards away, Haaland was, as best modern technology can measure, three centimeters behind the line of Dorgu's big toe.

Attackers with a special knack for staying onside often don't get as much love as they deserve. The most famous was probably AC Milan striker Filippo Inzaghi, whose high-wire style of play inspired Manchester United boss Sir Alex Ferguson to joke that the "lad must have been born offside."

Inzaghi took that personally. "Thankfully I was born a meter onside," he shot back, "otherwise I wouldn't have scored most of my goals."

Is it possible to measure who's really good or bad at staying onside -- and how much that skill is worth?

For an ability that can decide games or even titles, it's a little strange that we've never had an objective way to separate the Enzos and Haalands of the world. We obsess over players' goals and expected goals, but we rarely stop to wonder how many of those chances come from simply knowing how to stay on the right side of an invisible line.

One easy way to come at this missing measurement might be to count up a player's offside flags, but knowing that Haaland has been caught offside 25 times in the Premier League doesn't really tell us whether he's better or worse at it than Crystal Palace winger Ismaïla Sarr, who has the same number. Stats that aim to measure a skill need to account for the different levels of opportunity players have to do that thing.

So okay, fine, what about comparing offside flags to goals scored?

Now we might be getting somewhere. It's not exactly news that Haaland is a chart-warping statistical freak who piles up goals, but it's pretty mind-boggling to see that he's put up those numbers while being offside slightly less than Nottingham Forest wing back Daniel Muñoz.

What about the rest of the league, though? It's tough to say just from eyeballing this plot whether Palace's Jean-Philippe Mateta or Newcastle's Yoane Wissa is better at curving his runs. Trying to use a simple ratio of flags per goal doesn't really work, either. Midfielder Jorginho scored 21 goals for Chelsea and Arsenal while being offside exactly zero times, causing a calculator error that sounds impressive until you try to remember the last time you saw the flag go up on a penalty.

A better way to measure onside skill is to use detailed data on every touch of the ball. Witho

articles.headline: What NBA preseason has revealed about the Lakers, 76ers, Celtics and every team
articles.description: With 2026-27 tipoff closing in, Ben Golliver shares the key takeaways that will shape the regular season.
articles.body:
The NBA preseason is a time to welcome new faces, sort through lineup questions, hype up prospects, squabble over unresolved contract situations and panic about unfortunate injuries before the real competition begins.

With Tuesday's openers fast approaching, let's bounce around the league one final time in search of key takeaways that will shape the upcoming season.

Jump to a team:

ATL | BOS | BKN | CHA | CHI | CLE

DAL | DEN | DET | GS | HOU | IND

LAC | LAL | MEM | MIA | MIL | MIN

NO | NYK | OKC | ORL | PHI | PHX

POR | SAC | SA | TOR | UTAH | WAS

Atlanta Hawks

The preseason revealed ... the backcourt is loaded

With Trae Young's salary no longer on the books, the Hawks have assembled a backcourt rotation stacked with creators Nickeil Alexander-Walker and CJ McCollum, stoppers Dyson Daniels and Lu Dort, shooter Corey Kispert and 2026 lottery pick Kingston Flemings. In fact, Atlanta had such a surplus that it traded two backup guards to land 3-and-D forward Dorian Finney-Smith from the Charlotte Hornets in September.

Hawks coach Quin Snyder has used multiple starting lineups during the preseason, but he's best served sticking with last season's top group -- Alexander-Walker, McCollum, Daniels, Jalen Johnson and Onyeka Okongwu -- because it posted a phenomenal plus-20.3 net rating. That would move Dort to a reserve role after he spent the past six seasons as a starter for the Oklahoma City Thunder.

Boston Celtics

The preseason revealed ... Jayson Tatum will hit the ground running

While Tatum returned from a May 2025 Achilles tear in less than 10 months, his shot looked rusty and he played below his All-NBA standard down the stretch last season. Then, his speedy comeback ended with a whimper when he sat out a Game 7 loss to the Philadelphia 76ers in the first round due to left knee discomfort.

By taking those lumps last season, Tatum prepared himself for a smoother launch in 2026-27. The five-time All-Star was spectacular at times while posting 23 points in 27 minutes during his preseason debut, and his outside shot looked confident in a variety of situations. The Celtics must learn to live without Jaylen Brown and incorporate two key new pieces in forward Paul George and center Mitchell Robinson, but everything will be easier if Tatum is back to performing like an MVP contender.

Brooklyn Nets

The preseason revealed ... Egor Demin is one to watch

Be sure to include Demin on the list of 2025 first-round picks poised for major improvement in their second campaigns. While draft classmates in Dallas' Cooper Flagg and San Antonio's Dylan Harper are bursting with star potential, Demin's goal will be to move past a shaky rookie season and establish himself as a quality starting point guard.

articles.headline: Dembélé jokes he might ask for more holidays after PSG's win at Man City
articles.description: Ousmane Dembélé joked he might ask coach Luis Enrique for more time off after starring in PSG's 4-2 win at Manchester City in the Champions League.
articles.body:
Ousmane Dembélé joked he might ask coach Luis Enrique for more time off after starring in Paris Saint-Germain's 4-2 win at Manchester City in the Champions League.

The Ballon d'Or winner scored one goal and assisted on another in Wednesday's game. Luis Enrique had rested him after the recent international break, allowing Dembélé to sit out Saturday's home game against Le Mans, and he looked razor-sharp against City.

"After the international break I went on holiday. Actually, I might ask for more holidays," Dembélé told broadcaster Canal Plus. "I really enjoy playing on Tuesday and Wednesday, especially when I come back from holiday. It's a real pleasure."

Asked if he would go on holiday again, a smiling Dembélé added: "It's possible, until March I think. It's the coach who decides."

PSG have a trip to Strasbourg in Ligue 1 on Saturday, ahead of another high-profile Champions League game at home to Lamine Yamal's free-scoring Barcelona next Tuesday.

Luis Enrique may again rest players. He also omitted left-back Nuno Mendes against Le Mans, while Dembélé sat out a game against Lille in Ligue 1 earlier this season.

Dembélé won the French league's best player award last season, despite starting only nine games in PSG's title-winning campaign. The decision to award him the trophy over other players who played significantly more games led to criticism.

City coach Enzo Maresca said PSG enjoy a luxury his team and other Premier League sides don't have, being able to rotate players against modest Ligue 1 sides.

"They can manage players when they play games before the Champions League," he said. "For us, it's a bit different, especially when you go [to] Anfield."

City played Premier League rival Liverpool in a heated atmosphere on Sunday, giving Maresca's side one day less to prepare for the PSG game.

Last season, the French league accepted PSG's request to postpone their game against title rival Lens to allow better preparation for a Champions League quarterfinal against Liverpool -- a decision perceived by some observers as preferential treatment.

PSG went on to win the trophy for a second straight year, beating Arsenal on penalties in the final.

Dembélé has scored three Champions League goals, but has not yet found the net in four Ligue 1 matches this season. PSG are in sixth place after six rounds and some performances have fallen below expectations.

"We couldn't care less that people doubted us. We're in October, it's only the second game of the Champions League," he said. "We just need to stay on track during the first half of the season and prepare for the second."

However, he acknowledged PSG's concentration dropped off against City.

"We eased up a bit in the second half," Dembélé said. "When you do that against players like that, you pay for it."

articles.headline: 10 people who will define the NBA season: Zion, Kawhi, Kyrie
articles.description: With the NBA season just days away, let's take stock of the most important coaches, execs and players worth monitoring.
articles.body:
The 2025-26 NBA season is less than a week away, and while there are so many storylines surrounding the Philadelphia 76ers' present and the future of the NBA champion New York Knicks, there are several intriguing narratives around the league.

In some instances, it could take all season to shake out, while others could have a fate determined in the first quarter of the campaign.

Either way, here are 10 important people at all levels of the game who bear watching, starting with a No. 1 pick who is still looking to make his playoff debut.

Zion Williamson, New Orleans Pelicans

Why he's interesting: It's now or never, period.

Williamson's 62 games last season were the second most of his career, trailing only the 70 he played in 2022-23. His stretch of playing 52 of 53 games from Dec. 14 to April 5 was the longest such span of his career. The Pelicans were 21-31 during that time, as the team had a litany of players in and out through the season while trying to develop rookies Jeremy Fears and Derik Queen.

This is Year 8 for the 2019 No. 1 pick. The league moves fast, and Williamson's contract for 2027-28 is not guaranteed. Pelicans GM Troy Weaver previously went through the painstaking process of a Pistons rebuild at the start of the decade, with no assets to accrue draft capital, but that's not the case here. The new regime resisted wholesale changes last season, and they hope new coach Jamahl Mosley will have the same effect J.B. Bickerstaff had in Detroit three years ago before they make any drastic moves.

Williamson has the most credentials, but also the most questions. Apparently, he's come into camp in great shape, working plenty with assistant coach God Shammgod over the summer.

Doug Christie, Sacramento Kings

Why he's interesting: The bar isn't high.

There's no mandate for the Kings to make the playoffs with the current roster, and the front office has stated it would not saddle itself with win-now moves that jeopardize the future. Zach LaVine is on an expiring deal, and who knows how Domantas Sabonis, who has two years left on the extension he signed in 2023, fits into the future.

But Christie has yet to put an imprint on this roster as far as style of play, which is something Kings GM Scott Perry is big on. If Christie can put promising rookie point guard Darius Acuff Jr. in positions to be an elite lead performer, it will certainly be a feather in his cap while the roster starts to take shape. If it's another nondescript 22-win season with no discernible on-court quality, things could get tricky for the well-liked Christie.

 

LaMelo Ball, Minnesota Timberwolves

Why he's intriguing: The Timberwolves aren't strangers to big moves, going back to acquiring Rudy Gobert from the Utah Jazz for a cache of future picks and trading Karl-Anthony Towns to the Knicks two years ago, following their first trip to the Western Conference finals in 20 years.
